mostWorthwhile.text: Making silicate grains from oxygen-rich material and then joining them with metal grains was the most worthwhile passage: it connected stellar element production to the microscopic beginnings of rock.

leastWorthwhile.text: Checking the mixed element supply again and then trying to combine the two grain types led to dead ends. Those steps ruled out possibilities, but felt repetitive.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the stellar ejecta first drove a shock into surrounding gas rather than directly producing grains; the gas then had to radiate energy away.

arbitrary.text: The need to revisit carbon-rich stellar material and combine it with helium was not obvious from the dust goals, though the result explained the oxygen’s role.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the progression from stellar material to tiny grains was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how those grains contribute to planets.
